question.problem:
Evaluate the series ${\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }\frac{2}{{n}^{2}-7n+12}.$

*Hint: Try to factor the denominator first.*

${\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }\frac{2}{{n}^{2}-7n+12}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, factoring the denominator and using partial fractions, we can write the series as

$$
\frac{2}{{n}^{2}-7n+12}=\frac{2}{(n-4)(n-3)}=2(\frac{1}{n-4}-\frac{1}{n-3})
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
{\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }2(\frac{1}{n-4}-\frac{1}{n-3})=2{\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n-4}-\frac{1}{n-3}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{8} & =2[(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5})] \\ {s}_{9} & =2[(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{6})] \\ {s}_{10} & =2[(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{7})] \\ {s}_{11} & =2[(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{8})]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in each partial sum, we always end up canceling all terms except for the first and last terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=2(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N-3}).
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }\frac{2}{{n}^{2}-7n+12} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }2(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N-3}) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
